bank: EYES AND EARS -- E13 [half size check] -- THE UI SCALE AND TOUCH SWEEP, SPEC ONLY
round: 1 of 2 (SCHOOL). Nothing here has been built or run. Nothing was measured.
note: DRAFT MATERIAL, NEVER WIRED INTO THE GAME. School's two corrections: (1) 'did it halve' is not answerable by measuring the surface, because half of WHAT, and if no file holds the before then the ruling exists only as pixels and cannot be checked at all (E11's disease in a new lane). the_order_being_checked.words: for the run right now make all the UI 50% smaller, I don't give a fuck
the_order_being_checked.the_rule_that_survives: a control is DRAWN at half size while its invisible touch target stays 44 px
the_order_being_checked.status_when_school_ran: UI's [half size] row is CLAIMED, not shipped. this lane does not grade work that has not shipped.

the_four_bars.escape: five exceptions including a spacing offset: an undersized target passes if a 24 px circle centred on it hits nothing else

order_of_operations.how: a scale factor in a file (a --ui-scale custom property, a constant, a multiplier) is exact; else a ratio against git history; else declare it UNMEASURABLE and say the fix is a file, not a number
not two named ones: everything with a click handler, role=button, a pressable class, or a cursor that says it is pressable, across every frame, at 390x844

DRAWN via getBoundingClientRect in CSS px with the frame offset added; TOUCH via elementFromPoint walking outward from the centre until the point stops resolving to the control or a descendant; SPACING to the nearest other touch rectangle
clears AAA 44 / clears AA 24-with-spacing / clears neither. only the third is a defect. plus distance from screen centre, because Fitts needs it.
flag any control inside the top or bottom inset; a 44 px button under the home indicator is 44 px and unusable

why_drawn_is_not_touched.technique: position:relative on the control, an absolutely positioned ::after with a negative inset, wrapped in @media (pointer: coarse). a pseudo-element belongs to its parent so it acts as the parent's touch area, and unlike padding it does not touch the box model.
why_drawn_is_not_touched.status: standard and recommended; the CSS Working Group has an open issue (csswg-drafts 4708) asking for a first-class property, which says both that the need is real and that the hack is still how it is done
why_drawn_is_not_touched.consequence: getBoundingClientRect measures PAINT and cannot see a hit area at all. the sweep must hit-test.

the_prediction_to_verify_in_round_two.what_it_does: takes getBoundingClientRect() on two named controls (settext, setmotion) on one screen of the demo and fails on w < 44 || h < 44
the_prediction_to_verify_in_round_two.prediction_1: it measures the DRAWN box, so a control drawn at half size with an expanded invisible hit area -- exactly what the order asks for -- will turn it red on correct work. the order and the checker are pointed at each other.
the_prediction_to_verify_in_round_two.prediction_2: there is NO general touch-target sweep anywhere in this repo. the job says 'every touch target' and nothing in the fleet can currently answer 'every'.
the_prediction_to_verify_in_round_two.rule: this is a prediction and goes nowhere as a defect until round two has measured it; if it holds it is ONE [eyes: two words] line and nothing more.

rule_zero.the_trap: a subtly broken hit-test silently degrades into the old wrong check: it just returns the drawn box every time and looks plausible

controls.plant: a control drawn small WITH an expanded hit area
controls.must_measure: touch box BIGGER than drawn box

controls.plant: a control drawn small with NO expansion
controls.must_measure: touch box the SAME as drawn box

rule_zero.rule: if the first control does not separate, the instrument is measuring paint and every number it prints is void

ratchet.freeze: the count of controls that clear NEITHER bar

blind_spots_to_declare: one viewport and one device pixel ratio is not every phone
controls only reachable down a path the walk never takes are not enumerated
a control disabled or hidden at capture time is not the same as one that does not exist
this measures geometry, never whether the thing is legible; that is a different job with a different bar

the_real_world_half.fitts: time to acquire a target is a function of distance divided by size, and it holds for fingers, so halving a control has a price that grows with distance
the_real_world_half.thumb_zone: about 49% hold a phone one-handed and about 75% of interactions are thumb-driven (Hoober), BUT Hoober later argued the zone is not fixed: people change grip constantly and prefer to touch the CENTRE, where they tap fastest
the_real_world_half.consequence: round two does not score placement. it reports distance from centre because Fitts needs it, and stops there. a placement score would be enforcing lore its own author revised.

what_this_lane_may_not_do: change any UI size or touch target (this lane never writes game code)
decide what size anything should be (that is UI's and DIRECTION's, and the taste is his)
grade a row that has not shipped
